result.rationale: The line `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx does invalidate all bookings queries, but this is the standard, intentional cache-refresh pattern for tRPC mutations — after mutating a booking, the client must refetch booking data so the updated attendee list is reflected; broader invalidation here is a deliberate consistency mechanism, not a defect. The finding describes no incorrect behavior and the perf cost of an extra refetch of booking lists after a user-initiated mutation is a non-actionable nit (the data must be refetched anyway to show the new guests), so it fails

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the mutation `onSuccess` calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` with no args. In tRPC/React Query utils, invalidating a router path without specifying a procedure/input will invalidate all cached queries under `viewer.bookings`, potentially refetching multiple active booking lists even though only one booking (`bookingId`) changed. This is a concrete performance/scope concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.
